label: Timna

text.BHSA GEN 36:21: וְדִשֹׁ֥ון וְאֵ֖צֶר וְדִישָׁ֑ן אֵ֣לֶּה אַלּוּפֵ֧י הַחֹרִ֛י בְּנֵ֥י שֵׂעִ֖יר בְּאֶ֥רֶץ אֱדֹֽום׃
text.KJV GEN 36:21: And Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan: these are the dukes of the Horites, the children of Seir in the land of Edom.
text.BHSA GEN 36:22: וַיִּהְי֥וּ בְנֵי־לֹוטָ֖ן חֹרִ֣י וְהֵימָ֑ם וַאֲחֹ֥ות לֹוטָ֖ן תִּמְנָֽע׃
text.KJV GEN 36:22: And the children of Lotan were Hori and Hemam; and Lotan's sister was Timna.
text.BHSA GEN 36:23: וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ בְּנֵ֣י שֹׁובָ֔ל עַלְוָ֥ן וּמָנַ֖חַת וְעֵיבָ֑ל שְׁפֹ֖ו וְאֹונָֽם׃
text.KJV GEN 36:23: And the children of Shobal were these; Alvan, and Manahath, and Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.

A.name: Timna
A.line: concubine of Esau's son Eliphaz (GEN 36:12) and sister of Lotan (GEN 36:22)
family: mother-of amalek (Amalek, son of Eliphaz (GEN 36:12) and chief of Edom (GEN 36:16))
sister-of lotan (Lotan, son of Seir (GEN 36:20) and chief in Edom (GEN 36:29))

B.name: Timna
B.line: Daughter of Seir the Horite, sister of Lotan
family: sister-of lotan (Lotan, son of Seir (GEN 36:20) and chief in Edom (GEN 36:29))

why: The Hebrew וַאֲחוֹת לוֹטָן תִּמְנָע identifies Timna as Lotan’s sister within Seir’s genealogy, matching B. However, A states the same relationship, so the passage cannot securely distinguish these overlapping records; it names only one Timna.
